senses.definition: The visible part of fire; a stream of burning vapour or gas, emitting light and heat.
senses.example: Long after his cigar burnt bitter, he sat with eyes fixed on the blaze. When the flames at last began to flicker and subside, his lids fluttered, then drooped; but he had lost all reckoning of time when he opened them again to find Miss Erroll in furs and ball-gown kneeling on the hearth[…].

senses.definition: A romantic partner or lover in a usually short-lived but passionate affair.
senses.example: I could copy out yards of rhapsody to Lord George Poynings, her old flame, in which she addressed him by the most affectionate names.

senses.definition: An aggressively insulting criticism or remark.
senses.example: Flames are, unfortunately, a fact of USENET life. It's a rare USENET regular who hasn't been shaken to the foundations with anger at something some jerk has posted.

senses.definition: A brilliant reddish orange-gold fiery colour.
senses.example: [M]arked by myriad clouds of every sunset-colour - flame, purple, pink, green, violet, and all the tints of gold.

senses.definition:
A brilliant reddish orange-gold fiery colour.
flame:
The contrasting light and dark figure seen in wood used for stringed instrument making; the curl.
senses.example: The cello has a two-piece back with a beautiful narrow flame.

senses.definition: Burning zeal, passion, imagination, excitement, or anger.
senses.example: in a flame of zeal severe

The Gardeners divide it into Five Claſſes, which they diſtinguiſh by the Name of Picketees, Painted Ladies, Beazarts, Flakes, and Flames: […] the Flames have a red Ground always ſtrip’d with black or very dark Colours.

senses.definition: Of a brilliant reddish orange-gold colour, like that of a flame.
To produce flames; to burn with a flame or blaze.
senses.example: The main blaze of it is past, but a small thing would make it flame again.

senses.definition: To burst forth like flame; to break out in violence of passion; to be kindled with zeal or ardour.
To post a destructively critical or abusive message (to somebody).
senses.example: I flamed him for spamming in my favourite newsgroup.
